title: Generation of human parallel chimeric antigen receptor (pCAR) T cells
author: Larcombe-Young, Whilding, et al.

steps.title: Collect blood in heparin tubes
steps.instruction: Draw peripheral blood from consenting donors into 9 mL lithium‑heparin vacuette tubes.

steps.title: Calculate required blood volume
steps.instruction: Use the equation: Volume of blood (mL) = (Number of activated PBMCs needed × 10⁶ PBMCs / mL blood) × 2, assuming 1 × 10⁶ PBMCs per mL blood and a 50 % contingency loss.

steps.title: Pool and wash blood samples
steps.instruction: Combine the vacuette tubes into 50 mL Falcon tubes; wash each vacuette with 5 mL sterile PBS and add the wash to the pooled blood.

steps.title: Prepare Ficoll density gradient
steps.instruction: Aliquot 15 mL Ficoll‑Paque PLUS into each 50 mL Falcon tube (one tube per 35 mL whole blood). Keep the Ficoll tube horizontal, then layer 30 mL PBS‑diluted whole blood on top using a pipette aid and a 25 mL stripette, slowly reducing the tube angle until upright. Repeat until all blood is layered, using the pipette aid on the lowest speed to avoid mixing.

steps.title: Centrifuge for PBMC separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 800 × g for 35 min with brake and acceleration set to zero.

steps.title: Harvest PBMC layer
steps.instruction: Using a Pasteur pipette, carefully aspirate the PBMC layer (avoid drawing any Ficoll‑Paque PLUS) and transfer it to a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Dilute to final PBS volume
steps.instruction: Add sterile PBS to each tube to bring the total volume to 50 mL.

steps.title: First PBMC wash centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (≈20‑22 °C).

steps.title: Resuspend and combine pellets
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet, add 1 mL PBS to each pellet, resuspend, and combine all pellets into a single fresh 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Second PBMC wash
steps.instruction: Wash the combined cells with 5 mL sterile PBS, then centrifuge again at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (≈20‑22 °C).

steps.title: Final centrifugation of PBMCs
steps.instruction: Aspirate the PBS carefully, leaving the cell pellet untouched.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in R5 medium
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL R5 medium (RPMI + 2 mM L‑glutamine + 5 % human male AB serum).

steps.title: Count cells with trypan blue
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of the PBMC suspension with 10 µL trypan blue and count viable cells using a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the cells with R5 medium to a final concentration of 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

steps.title: Seed cells into 6‑well plates
steps.instruction: Plate 4 mL of the cell suspension per well in tissue‑culture‑treated 6‑well plates (3‑100 million PBMCs can be activated this way).

steps.title: Add PHA‑L activation reagent
steps.instruction: Add phytohemagglutinin‑L to each well to achieve a final concentration of 5 µg/mL and mix well.

steps.title: Incubate and add IL‑2
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 48 h without changing medium. After 24 h, add 100 IU/mL recombinant human IL‑2 to the activated PBMCs.

substeps.instruction: Do not change or add medium during the 48 h incubation, as medium becomes conditioned with cytokines from activated T cells.

steps.title: Optional T‑cell isolation and activation
steps.instruction: If needed, isolate T cells from the PBMC fraction using the Miltenyi Pan T‑cell Isolation Kit (manufacturer’s protocol). For purified T cells, activate with CD3/CD28 Human T‑Activator Dynabeads™ or T‑cell Transact™ according to the respective manufacturer’s instructions.
